code_quality.description: PersistentFailureHints generates a message format that doesn't match the spec-required format. The spec mandates: `"persistent-failure: <key> has failed N consecutive cycles — may indicate a bad test specification rather than an implementation bug"`. The implementation generates: `"persistent-failure: <name> (occurred N times across consecutive cycles; bad test specification suspected)"`. Any downstream parsing or display logic targeting the canonical spec wording will not match.
code_quality.suggested_fix: Update the fmt.Sprintf format string to match the spec exactly: `"persistent-failure: %s has failed %d consecutive cycles — may indicate a bad test specification rather than an implementation bug"`

code_quality.description: writeTestFile writes all test files as flat files under workDir root (`<workDir>/<safe-scenario-name>_test.go`), completely ignoring the package structure of the code under test. The spec requires test files be placed "in the same package as the code under test" (e.g., `calc/calc_scenario_add_test.go`). The LLM response contains a `package <name>` declaration, but the adapter never parses it to determine the correct subdirectory. Test files will be placed in the wrong directory, causing `go test ./...` in the correct package to miss them entirely.
code_quality.suggested_fix: Parse the `package` declaration from the LLM response to determine the target subdirectory, or require the LLM to return a structured response that includes the intended file path alongside the content.

code_quality.description: `implFiles []string` is formatted with `%v` in the prompt template, producing Go slice syntax `[file1.go file2.go]`. This is awkward in a natural-language prompt and may confuse the LLM. A newline-separated list or comma-separated list would be clearer.
code_quality.suggested_fix: Use `strings.Join(implFiles, "\n")` instead of `%v` for a cleaner natural-language rendering.

code_quality.description: File contains only `package contract` with no other content. The `ScenarioTestWriter` interface was placed in `types.go` instead. This empty file adds noise, implies the interface should be here, and confuses readers about where the interface is defined.
code_quality.suggested_fix: Delete the empty file. The interface is already correctly placed in types.go.

code_quality.description: `Store *runstore.Store` is stored in `WriteScenarioTestsStageConfig` and accepted by `NewWriteScenarioTestsStage`, but is never accessed anywhere in the `Run` method. Dead field that widens the constructor signature unnecessarily.
code_quality.suggested_fix: Remove the `Store` field from `WriteScenarioTestsStageConfig` and the corresponding parameter from `NewWriteScenarioTestsStage`. Update call sites in `stage_provider.go`.

code_quality.description: `type Scenario = ScenarioTestManifestEntry` is declared with a comment claiming it exists "for backward compatibility", but this is entirely new code with no prior version. The alias introduces two names for the same type in the same package, causing confusion about which to use. Other parts of the file already use `ScenarioTestManifestEntry` directly.
code_quality.suggested_fix: Remove the alias and use `ScenarioTestManifestEntry` consistently throughout the file.

code_quality.description: The re-run skip logic only checks whether a scenario name appears in the manifest (`writtenScenarios[scenario.Name]`) but does not verify the corresponding test file still exists on disk or compiles. The spec explicitly requires: "if the test file exists and compiles, it is skipped. If it exists but does not compile, it is deleted and re-written." A test file deleted or corrupted between runs will be silently skipped, leaving a broken test in the manifest.
code_quality.suggested_fix: Before skipping, stat the file at `manifest.Scenarios[i].TestFile`; if missing, remove it from the skip set. Optionally also run the compile check and delete+re-add to the write queue if it fails.

code_quality.description: The `implFiles` collection loop appends all `task.FilesChanged` slices without deduplication. If multiple tasks list the same file, it appears multiple times in the prompt sent to the LLM. The spec says the input should be a "deduplicated union from per-task `FilesChanged`".
code_quality.suggested_fix: Use a `map[string]struct{}` to deduplicate before building the `implFiles` slice.

code_quality.description: `mockScenarioTestWriter` in the specloop integration test has a `scenarios []string` field that is never populated or read. The mock itself is immediately discarded with `_ = mockWriter` at line ~314, making the entire struct definition dead code. This mock provides zero test coverage of the skip-on-partial-manifest behavior it was presumably created to exercise.
code_quality.suggested_fix: Remove the unused `scenarios []string` field. If `TestIntegration_PartialCompletion_SkipsCompiledScenarios` is intended to test the real stage, wire it through `NewWriteScenarioTestsStage` with an injected mock rather than discarding it.

code_quality.description: `createMockPipelineStages()` omits the "compile" stage that exists in the real pipeline (`BuildStages` returns init, compile, plan, write_contracts, execute, write_scenario_tests, validate, review, accept, evidence, finalize). `TestIntegration_PipelineStageOrder` validates order against this hardcoded mock, so it won't catch a reordering that affects compile's position, and its stage count diverges from the real pipeline making the test misleading.
code_quality.suggested_fix: Add `&namedStage{name: "compile"}` at index 1 to match the real pipeline, or add a count assertion to catch future divergence.

code_quality.description: In `TestWriteScenarioTests_CompileFailureExhausted`, the assertion that the blocked reason mentions "repair attempts" uses `t.Logf` (a non-failing log call) instead of `t.Errorf`. The test passes regardless of the actual reason content, providing false confidence that the failure message is correct.
code_quality.suggested_fix: Change `t.Logf("warning: blocked event reason doesn't mention repair attempts: %s", be.Reason)` to `t.Errorf(...)` so the assertion actually enforces the expected message content.

code_quality.description: `executeIdx`, `writeScenarioTestsIdx`, and `validateIdx` are all initialized to zero. If `write_scenario_tests` or `validate` are absent from the mock pipeline, the guards `if writeScenarioTestsIdx == 0` and `if validateIdx == 0` catch this. However there is no guard for `executeIdx == 0`, so a missing `execute` stage silently leaves `executeIdx = 0` (pointing at `init`), and the ordering assertion `writeScenarioTestsIdx <= executeIdx` could produce a confusing/misleading failure or false pass.
code_quality.suggested_fix: Add `if executeIdx == 0 { t.Fatal("execute stage not found in pipeline") }` alongside the other guards.

code_quality.description: `FailureHistory` field has inconsistent alignment compared to `ScenarioTestsWritten` directly above it. `ScenarioTestsWritten` has trailing spaces for column-aligned struct tags; `FailureHistory` does not, making the struct visually inconsistent.
code_quality.suggested_fix: Align `FailureHistory map[string]int` to match the column alignment of adjacent fields using tabs, consistent with the rest of the struct.

code_quality.description: `TestIntegration_PartialCompletion_SkipsCompiledScenarios` does not invoke `WriteScenarioTestsStage.Run` at all. It manually populates a `map[string]bool`, validates that map logic, then discards the `mockScenarioTestWriter` with `_ = mockWriter`. The test provides zero coverage of the actual skip-on-partial-manifest behavior in the real stage's `Run` method.
code_quality.suggested_fix: Either rewrite the test to construct a real `WriteScenarioTestsStage` with a pre-populated manifest and verify the writer is called only for the unwritten scenario, or remove it and rely on `TestWriteScenarioTests_PartialManifestSkip` in the stages package which correctly exercises this.

spec_alignment.description: PersistentFailureHints generates a message that does not match the spec-required format. The spec mandates: `"persistent-failure: <key> has failed N consecutive cycles — may indicate a bad test specification rather than an implementation bug"`. The implementation produces: `"persistent-failure: <key> (occurred N times across consecutive cycles; bad test specification suspected)"`. The wording diverges significantly — missing `"has failed"`, using `"occurred"` instead, and different phrasing for the diagnostic hint. Any downstream code or documentation that pattern-matches on the spec's canonical phrase will not find it.
spec_alignment.suggested_fix: Change the format string to: `fmt.Sprintf("persistent-failure: %s has failed %d consecutive cycles — may indicate a bad test specification rather than an implementation bug", key, count)`

spec_alignment.description: writeTestFile places the generated test file directly in the root of workDir (`filepath.Join(workDir, safeScenarioName+"_test.go")`), completely ignoring package structure. The spec requires: "File placement: Same package as the code under test" (e.g., `calc/calc_scenario_add_test.go`). Since the LLM response contains a `package <name>` declaration, the adapter needs to parse that declaration or otherwise determine the correct subdirectory. Tests written to the wrong directory will fail both compilation in the package check and `go test ./...` in the target package.
spec_alignment.suggested_fix: Parse the `package` declaration from the LLM response to determine the subdirectory, then write to `filepath.Join(workDir, pkgName, filename)`. Alternatively, require the LLM to return the target path as a separate field.

spec_alignment.description: Implementation files are formatted with `%v` (`%v` applied to `implFiles []string`), which produces `[file1.go file2.go]` — Go's default slice rendering with brackets. This is awkward in a natural-language prompt and may confuse the LLM about which files are relevant. The prompt section reads `Implementation Files (changed by tasks):\n%v`.
spec_alignment.suggested_fix: Format the list as a newline-separated bullet list: `strings.Join(implFiles, "\n")` or `"- " + strings.Join(implFiles, "\n- ")`.

spec_alignment.description: `WriteScenarioTestsStageConfig` holds a `Store *runstore.Store` field that is wired in `NewWriteScenarioTestsStage` but never accessed anywhere in the `Run` method. Dead field that adds noise to the config struct and misleads readers about what resources the stage uses.
spec_alignment.suggested_fix: Remove `Store *runstore.Store` from `WriteScenarioTestsStageConfig` and the corresponding parameter from `NewWriteScenarioTestsStage`, or document a planned use.

spec_alignment.description: `type Scenario = ScenarioTestManifestEntry` is declared with a comment claiming it exists "for backward compatibility", but this is entirely new code with no prior version. The alias introduces two exported names for the same type within the same package, causing confusion about which name to use. There is no backward compatibility rationale in new code.
spec_alignment.suggested_fix: Remove the alias and use `ScenarioTestManifestEntry` consistently throughout the file, or rename `ScenarioTestManifestEntry` to `Scenario` directly.

spec_alignment.description: The re-run skip logic only checks whether a scenario name appears in the partial manifest (`writtenScenarios[scenario.Name]`), but does not verify that the corresponding test file actually exists on disk or still compiles. The spec requires: "if the test file exists and compiles, it is skipped. If it exists but does not compile, it is deleted and re-written." A test file that was deleted or corrupted between runs will be silently skipped rather than regenerated.
spec_alignment.suggested_fix: After finding a scenario in the manifest, stat the file and attempt compilation. If the file is missing or fails to compile, delete it from the manifest entry and proceed to re-write.

spec_alignment.description: The implementation files collection does not deduplicate entries. If multiple tasks list the same file in `FilesChanged`, it appears multiple times in `implFiles`. The spec explicitly requires a "deduplicated union from per-task `FilesChanged`". Duplicate entries bloat the prompt sent to the LLM.
spec_alignment.suggested_fix: Use a map to deduplicate: collect files into a `map[string]struct{}`, then convert to slice.

spec_alignment.description: The file contains only `package contract` with no other content. The `ScenarioTestWriter` interface was placed in `types.go` instead. This empty file adds confusion about interface ownership and serves no purpose.
spec_alignment.suggested_fix: Either move the `ScenarioTestWriter` interface declaration here (its natural home given the filename) or delete this file.

spec_alignment.description: `executeIdx`, `writeScenarioTestsIdx`, and `validateIdx` are all initialized to zero. If the `write_scenario_tests` or `execute` stages are not found in the pipeline, their indices remain 0. The ordering assertion `writeScenarioTestsIdx <= executeIdx` (checking `N <= 0`) then gives a misleading error unrelated to ordering. A missing `execute` stage (index stays 0) would cause `writeScenarioTestsIdx (4) <= executeIdx (0)` to be false — the test would pass rather than failing with a clear "stage not found" error.
spec_alignment.suggested_fix: Add explicit guards: `if executeIdx == 0 { t.Fatal("execute stage not found") }` after the loop, before the ordering checks.

spec_alignment.description: `TestIntegration_PartialCompletion_SkipsCompiledScenarios` does not test the `WriteScenarioTestsStage` at all. It manually builds a map, validates the map logic, then discards the `mockScenarioTestWriter` with `_ = mockWriter`. The test provides zero coverage of the actual manifest-based skip logic in `WriteScenarioTestsStage.Run`. This is covered properly in `write_scenario_tests_test.go:TestWriteScenarioTests_PartialManifestSkip`.
spec_alignment.suggested_fix: Either delete this test (since the real coverage exists elsewhere) or replace the body with an invocation of the actual `WriteScenarioTestsStage` with a pre-populated manifest.

spec_alignment.description: `FailureHistory map[string]int` lacks the column alignment applied to adjacent fields. `ScenarioTestsWritten bool` uses trailing spaces for tag alignment; `FailureHistory` does not, breaking the visual consistency of the struct definition.

`TestIntegration_ScenarioTestsWritten_PreventRegeneration` tests `mockWriteScenarioTestsStage`, a hand-rolled mock that hardcodes the idempotency guard — not the actual `WriteScenarioTestsStage`. The test validates the mock's own logic, not the production implementation. The real idempotency behavior is already tested in `write_scenario_tests_test.go:TestWriteScenarioTests_IdempotencyGuard` against the actual stage. This integration test adds no coverage value.
spec_alignment.suggested_fix: Replace the mock with an actual `WriteScenarioTestsStage` instantiation (using a spec with scenarios, a `fakeScenarioTestWriter`, and a temp dir), mirroring how `TestWriteScenarioTests_HappyPath` is structured.

spec_alignment.description: In `TestWriteScenarioTests_HappyPath` and several other tests, the mock writer returns a relative path `"test_scenario.go"`. `filepath.Dir("test_scenario.go")` returns `"."`, so the default `compileChecker` runs `go test -c -o /dev/null .` in `cmd.Dir = "."` — which is the `stages` package directory during testing. This always succeeds because the `stages` package is valid Go, regardless of the scenario test content. The compile check in these tests is therefore a no-op that provides false confidence about the self-repair loop.
spec_alignment.suggested_fix: In tests that exercise compile success, inject a `compileChecker` stub via `stage.compileChecker = func(...) (string, error) { return "", nil }` rather than relying on the default checker with a relative path, making the test intent explicit.
